question.text: The J.R. Verma Committee is best known for its recommendations on which aspect of derivative market regulation?

answer.text: Risk management framework including margining methodology for exchange-traded derivatives
The overall regulatory framework, governance structure, and membership criteria for derivative exchanges
Tax treatment and stamp duty norms for derivative transactions
Investor grievance redressal and arbitration mechanisms for derivative market disputes

explanation.text: The Logic: The J.R. Verma Committee, set up by SEBI, is conventionally associated in Indian derivative market history with the risk-management and margining framework for exchange-traded derivatives, including recommendations on initial margin computation, mark-to-market settlement and portfolio-based (SPAN-style) margining used by Indian clearing corporations. The Trap: The broader regulatory-framework recommendations (governance structure, membership criteria, net worth, etc.) are conventionally associated with the L.C. Gupta Committee, not Verma. Tax/stamp-duty rules and investor grievance/arbitration mechanisms are governed by separate statutory and SEBI frameworks, not by Verma. Note: The "J.R. Verma Committee" attribution was not located in the cited workbook pages (Currency p.192-p.193; IR p.230; Equity p.160-p.161); those pages cover RBI-SEBI committee terms and SPAN margining mechanics. The framing above relies on general Indian derivative-market regulatory history rather than a workbook citation.
